name: Agility Robotics Digit 5
description: The fifth generation of Agility Robotics' warehouse-and-logistics humanoid, unveiled September 15, 2026 as a near-total redesign: human-like forward-bending knees replace the bird-inspired reverse-knee legs Digit has used since 2017, payload rises to 50 lb, and a fast-charge battery targets a 10:1 run-to-charge ratio for roughly 20 hours of daily work. It isn't shipping yet — early access starts in H1 2027 — and every Digit currently working at a customer site today is still the prior Digit 4.

specs.label: Battery
specs.note: 9 min fast recharge; ~10:1 run-to-charge ratio claimed

specs.label: Compute
specs.note: plus NVIDIA Halos safety framework; degrees of freedom unconfirmed by Agility

specs.label: Legs
specs.note: replaces the bird-inspired reverse-knee design Digit used since 2017

specs.label: Hands
specs.note: not a dexterous humanoid hand — true of every Digit generation

specs.label: Availability
specs.note: early access H1 2027; general availability late 2027

sourcing: Verified against Agility's own Digit 5 announcement and product page, PR Newswire, The Robot Report ("The Evolution of Digit" retrospective and its Digit 5 legs/battery/safety coverage), GeekWire, Forbes, TechRepublic, Businesswire's SPAC merger announcement, Contrary Research, TechCrunch's 2024 layoffs reporting, an independent SEC-filing analysis (digidai.github.io), and Automate.org. Flagged as lower-confidence or unconfirmed: the reported ~$400M/~$1.8B Series C figures; a ~16 degrees-of-freedom figure cited only by a third-party aggregator; the $8,500/month RaaS rate and ~$250,000 purchase price, both analyst estimates rather than Agility-confirmed pricing; and the "$300M+ in orders" headline, which traces to one conditional, related-party contract rather than diversified demand. This entry's tier remains "pending" because Digit 5 itself has not shipped to any customer as of this research.

pricing.summary: No public price exists for Digit 5, or for any Digit generation — Agility sells only through negotiated enterprise contracts, generally structured as Robots-as-a-Service (RaaS) rather than a purchase. Analyst estimates for the RaaS rate on the prior Digit 4 generation cluster around $8,500 per robot per month, and a roughly $250,000 one-time purchase price was reported for an early Digit unit around 2020, but neither figure is confirmed by Agility for Digit 5.

editorial.heading: Insights
editorial.body: TechCrunch reported Amazon's Digit pilots "ended without announced next steps" around a round of Agility layoffs, and Agility's own 2026 SPAC filings describe Amazon only as "an active pilot partner," not a paying customer — treat any claim that Amazon is a current Digit customer with caution. Agility's claim of being "the first humanoid to pass an OSHA-recognized safety evaluation" is also real but narrower than it sounds — it covers only a site-specific Digit 4 field test, not Digit 5 or any finalized industry safety standard.

firmwareCommunity.note: Agility Robotics Digit 5 has not released a public SDK, firmware repo, or developer API; the only related public code found is a third-party ROS 2 workspace that installs a private "agility-pysdk" wheel to talk to Agility's own JSON API — not an official SDK or resource. Not currently listed in Builds & Mods.
